notes: `upstream` is the base image the extended Dockerfile FROMs — the Isol8 fork (Isol8AI/agent) built from upstream OpenClaw 2026.7.2 (branch off tag v2026.7.2-beta.3 — 7.2 is BETA-ONLY upstream, no stable cut yet) plus the FOUR carried fork patches. Three are re-expressed onto 7.2's rewritten MCP manager (upstream #106359): bundled-MCP shared-runtime-scope (keys the static runtime on (workspaceDir, agentDir, configFingerprint) so sessions reuse one connected runtime — collapses the per-session EFS connect storm), non-blocking tool materialization (peek-then-warm; a cold catalog streams the run on built-ins and warms MCP in the background), and provider-agnostic size-based context pruning (Isol8AI/agent#1). The FOURTH, new in isol8.2, is the native workspace-seed boot hook: `ensureAgentWorkspace` converts an Isol8 sentinel `.openclaw/isol8-setup-seed.json` into native SQLite workspace-setup-state via OpenClaw's own `mergeWorkspaceSetupState`, then deletes the sentinel — so no legacy `workspace-state.json` is ever written and the #1429 "requires migration" brick class is structurally impossible. It is INERT when no sentinel exists (zero behavior change for existing containers), non-throwing (a failure logs and falls through to normal boot), and kill-switched by env `ISOL8_NATIVE_SETUP_SEED=0`. The 7.1 compaction aws-sdk-auth cherry-pick (openclaw#103638) was DROPPED — native in beta.3. REQUIRED to build the extended image FROM this fork tag, NOT vanilla ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw: config.py emits mcp.runtimeScope="shared" which only the shared-runtime-scope patch adds to the strict config schema (McpConfigSchema, relocated to zod-schema.root-support.ts in #106359, still `z.strictObject`) — a vanilla 7.2 base crash-loops every MCP owner and (via 7.x's fail-closed startup-migration checkpoint) fails the whole fleet closed. Tag scheme `<upstream-version>-isol8.<n>`. This is a PRIVATE GHCR package, only pulled by the authenticated build-openclaw-image.yml workflow. DEPLOY POSTURE: 7.2 is beta upstream; prod has been on beta by explicit owner acceptance since 2026-07-20. `dev.tag` and `prod.tag` are both `2026.7.2-isol8.2-d5e1aed` — the extended image built from merge d5e1aed (PR #1495), which rewrites ONLY the isol8 SKILL.md frontmatter `description` so it leads with email and names the dead ends (no Gmail, no himalaya, no OpenClaw email channel). A prod run had an agent asked to email its owner go hunting for those transports and conclude none was configured — it never opened the skill, because the old description named surfaces and billing but never the word "email". The send path itself was already shipped and unchanged; this is a discovery fix. Both envs pinned together by explicit owner decision. Roll back to `2026.7.2-isol8.2-fc10c0c` if needed — the change is copy-only, so a rollback costs nothing but the discoverability. `image`/`tag`/`full` are the LEGACY PUBLIC upstream image (ghcr.io/openclaw/openclaw): container-stack.ts uses `full` as the bootstrap/unknown-env fallback, pulled by per-user ECS tasks that carry NO registry credentials — so it must stay anonymously pullable and must NOT point at the private fork. `tag` also feeds the OPENCLAW_UPSTREAM_VERSION env-var fallback. `extendedImage` + per-env `dev.tag`/`prod.tag` are the ECR-published extended image deployed to dev and prod. PROMOTION IS MANUAL: build-openclaw-image.yml only READS this file and prints "Bump openclaw-version.json#dev.tag to <tag> in a PR to deploy to dev" to its job summary — it never writes the tags. A green image build therefore ships NOTHING to any container until a human lands a PR flipping these fields (an earlier revision of this note wrongly claimed the workflow re-stamps them, which cost a debugging cycle).
